archetype: Five-colour legendary-permanent toolbox. strategic_frame.json calls it exactly that, and the audit agrees by declining to name an archetype at all — base targets apply, so every template figure below is a starting point rather than a verdict. The deck's currency is access: Sisay, Weatherlight Captain is a repeatable, self-escalating battlefield tutor whose gate widens as the board's colour count grows.
verdict: The mana works and the commander lands: 93.5% turn-3 land drops, zero unconditional taplands, commander cast a mean 2.963 and 99.1% by turn 6. What limits the deck is conversion. threat-density counts three finishers and none of Boros Charm, Kambal or Samut closes three opponents; the only checker-passed kill in the deck is stack 002's Najeela + Derevi combat loop, which needs {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} every single combat — the same five-pip, zero-generic cost Sisay's own activation needs. One resource gates both the engine and the only verified win, and 17 of the deck's 55 mana sources cannot pay it.

components.reading: The pip battery, and the real bottleneck. Six cards, 36.4% of openers, 67.9% assembled and only 55.8% by turn 6 — so in nearly half of games the deck reaches turn 6 with a tutor it cannot repeatedly activate. Three of the six (Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Relic of Legends) are non-legendary and therefore invisible to Sisay herself.

Seven cards, 41.2% of openers, 74.7% assembled at a mean turn 2.836 — this is why the commander lands on turn 2.963. It does its job. Two of the seven, Sol Ring and Delighted Halfling, cannot contribute a single pip to what the commander does next.

Eleven cards, 57.4% of openers, 88.4% assembled at mean turn 2.3 — the deck's healthiest component. Nine of the eleven are non-legendary, so this is the class the tutor can never go and get; it has to be drawn, which is exactly why it is built wide.

single_points_of_failure.why: Sisay's activation is five coloured pips with zero generic, and Najeela's untap — the payment step of the one checker-passed kill — is the identical cost, once per combat. The declared proxy for having it assembles in 67.9% of games and 55.8% by turn 6, and 6 cards is the whole redundancy behind it. Nothing else in the deck substitutes: Sol Ring, Delighted Halfling and Unclaimed Territory cannot pay any part of it.

lean_into.why: Commander mean cast turn 2.963, 99.1% by turn 6, on 0.183 mean mulligans, with protection available in 88.4% of games at mean turn 2.3. Both halves of commander insurance are already paid for; the recast tax is the thing to avoid, not the thing to plan around.

lean_into.what: Buy answers virtually, through the fetchable tax shell, instead of counting removal spells.
lean_into.why: The interaction axis reads exactly 8 and six of those are counterspells, which looks thin. It undercounts what the deck actually does: Thalia, Heretic Cathar, Kutzil, Teferi, Time Raveler, Kambal and Sheoldred are all legendary, all mana value 2-4, and all sit inside the fetch pool once the ladder reaches two or three colours. One of them blanks plans at three seats at once, and Sisay can go and get it on demand.

lean_into.what: Treat Najeela + Derevi as the plan, and count its requirements out loud.
lean_into.why: It is the only line in this deck a checker has passed. Stack 002's own verdict is that it is 'a genuine, deterministic, unbounded combat loop, but not a self-contained two-card infinite' — it needs a manabase producing {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} every combat and at least five creatures connecting, and it only breaks even on combat 2. Both pieces are mana value 3 and therefore fetchable once the ladder reaches two colours.

This is a genuine loss and the recommendation stands anyway: an answer you cannot cast on curve and cannot tutor for is not an answer you can plan on.

open_questions.question: Can a legend Sisay puts onto the battlefield this turn be tapped to pay for the next activation — via Relic of Legends' cost, or via the '{T}: Add one mana of any color' Esika grants it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the deck chains fetches inside one turn or across two, which is the difference between a tutor and an engine. Stack 003 argues Relic works and Esika's grant does not, but its checker verdict is fail on the iteration bound, so nothing here is fact.

open_questions.question: Does Mikaeus, the Lunarch arrive as a 0/0 and die immediately when put onto the battlefield by Sisay rather than cast, since X is never chosen?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Mikaeus is one of only three mana value 1 or less legendary permanents in the deck. If he is not a live target at Sisay's base power 2, the cold-start pool is two cards, not three, and the opening-turn sequencing advice changes.

open_questions.question: Should the 'Sisay online with a three-colour legend to grow her' target be re-declared as any two legendary permanents of differing colours?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Sisay's power counts distinct colours among OTHER legendary permanents, and 33 of them qualify — the declared four-card group is one shortcut to power 5, not the requirement. Its 52.5% assembled rate is currently the thinnest figure in the audit, and it may be measuring the wrong question.

open_questions.question: Do Jodah, the Unifier's anthem and Flowering of the White Tree's +2/+1 raise Sisay's power for the purpose of her own fetch gate?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Her gate reads mana value less than her power, not less than her colour count. If power boosts widen it, the deck's ceiling is not power 6, and any future card above mana value 5 becomes reachable.

open_questions.question: Does Najeela plus a single omni-mana body — Faeburrow Elder, Esika, or Selvala, Heart of the Wilds — loop without Derevi?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Three bracket-3 lines that would each give the verified kill a second assembly path off cards already in the 99. Stack 002 proved the Derevi version needs five different colours re-produced every combat; whether one permanent can supply that is the whole question.

open_questions.question: Does Walking Ballista plus Heliod, Sun-Crowned close the game in this deck?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the justification for the threat-density add above. Until a checker passes it, the deck would still have exactly one verified kill and the recommendation is a bet rather than a fix.

open_questions.question: Does the escalating Sisay activation chain in stack 001 hold, and can a fetch be re-chosen if a colour-contributing legend is removed in response?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 001 is the deck's core sequencing document and its checker verdict is fail on the iteration bound with one unresolved finding at step 11. The pilot is making these decisions every turn on an artifact that did not pass.

gaps: No deck_recon.json exists for this deck (deck-audit freshness.recon.present is false), so nothing here is grounded in what strong Sisay lists actually run. Inclusion-rate evidence would change which of the four adds is ranked first.

No archetype is established, so every axis target is a base template rather than a fitted one. strategy:deckbuilding.ratios is explicit that its counts should come from the deck's actual failure modes.
9 of the 10 combo lines fully contained in the 99 are unadjudicated. Only stack 002 is checker-passed; stacks 001 and 003 read fail.

upgrade-facts' synergy channel returned only ramp:cost-reduction cards for this deck and surfaced no candidate for the thinnest engine component. The channel is a format-wide top-10 shortlist, not a fit score, and it found nothing usable here.

The obsolescence index proposes Elvish Mystic as an upgrade to both Bloom Tender and Faeburrow Elder on similarity 0.9755 and 0.9667. It is format-agnostic and does not know that this deck buys those two cards for five-colour output, not for a green mana; the recommendation is wrong and is recorded here rather than acted on.
DECK_ROLE_BUDGET's shortfalls (draw 4, sweeper 2, tutor 1, wincon 1) are labelled provisional and uncited by upgrade-facts itself and were not used as evidence anywhere above.
The deck has no sideboard, so every add is a pool proposal with no owned-card evidence behind it.
